name: Star Badge
defects: Extra side appendage on the right: a small round disk/knob and short horizontal bar protrude from behind the badge, with no matching part on the left.
The right-side appendage appears embedded or fused into the star edge rather than attached like a real badge pin or clasp.
Outer points and ball tips are slightly asymmetric in length and placement.

name: Iron Stove
defects: Top vent slots are unevenly shaped and spaced, with some looking warped rather than cleanly cut.
Chimney elbow appears fused into the top rim/body instead of being a clearly separate pipe connection.
Legs are asymmetrical: the front legs and rear/right leg have different shapes and sizes, and a small central rear stump-like leg is visible under the body.
Door/hinge area is slightly melted together; the hinge blocks blend into the door frame and body rather than having clear separations.

name: Deputy Boots
defects: Pull tabs/loops are placed on the front/back of the boot openings instead of as side pull straps, making the construction unrealistic.
Spur assemblies attach to side buttons/straps rather than wrapping around the back of the heels with a proper yoke.
Left boot spur is partly hidden and appears only loosely connected to the boot.
The two boots have noticeably different visible spur placement and hardware shape/position.

name: Jail Keys
defects: The blue key heads overlap in the center and appear partially fused/penetrating each other rather than clearly separate pieces on the ring.
The thick blue key ring has no visible split or opening, making it unclear how the keys or charm could be added or removed.
The gold charm connector uses a very thin pale line that looks like a floating wire/string rather than a solid linked metal part, and it is not clearly attached to the star charm.
The gold loop and small bead near the charm look blobbed together, with unclear separation between connector parts.

name: Stagecoach
defects: Front pull shafts are not clearly connected to a central hitch or front axle; they appear to grow from the underside/side of the coach.
Visible wheels are inconsistent: two large near-side wheels plus a much smaller partial far-side wheel, making the wheel layout look uneven.
Wheel axles are mostly missing or hidden; the wheels appear attached directly to the body rather than to a clear axle structure.
Driver/front seat is fused into the side/front body with no clear footboard or support structure.
Roof railing posts and luggage slightly merge together in places.

name: Hitching Rail
defects: Horizontal rail appears to merge into the side faces of both posts instead of passing through visible holes or being held by brackets.
Left and right posts are noticeably different in proportions: the left post is thicker/taller with a larger cap, while the right post is slimmer and shaped differently.
Decorative ring bands around the posts are uneven and look molded/fused into the posts rather than separate clean pieces.
Horizontal rail is slightly warped and changes thickness along its length.

name: Quiet Cell
defects: Lock is mounted on the front bars with no visible hasp or latch connecting it to the wooden frame, so it would not actually lock the door.
Left-side hinges appear as short metal cylinders attached to or floating beside the bars, without proper hinge leaves connecting the door to the wooden frame.
Several vertical bars have unclear/warped connections to the top and bottom horizontal rails, appearing to pass through or end behind them inconsistently.
The front barred door and the surrounding wooden frame are not clearly separated, making the opening/door construction physically ambiguous.

name: Lasso
defects: Main loop is not a clearly continuous single rope; it appears as multiple parallel rope tubes fused together.
Knot construction is impossible/ambiguous, with rope segments merging into smooth blobs instead of passing over and under correctly.
The hanging loop/tail grows out of the knot in an unclear way and does not trace as one continuous rope.
Several rope sections on the right side intersect or fuse rather than remaining separate strands.

name: Bedroll
defects: buckle tongues are simplified/fused into the buckles and do not appear to pass through real strap holes
front buckle straps are not clearly threaded through the buckles; they look like separate decorative plates attached on top
top patterned flap blends into the rolled side with unclear fabric layering

name: Trail Saddle
defects: Two stirrups/straps appear to hang from the same visible side instead of one on each side of the saddle.
The front/left stirrup strap attaches near the middle-front of the saddle rather than from the side fender position.
The two stirrups and their straps are noticeably different sizes and shapes.
The wooden stand has a side support/block protruding oddly through or into the saddle pad area on the left.
Some saddle parts are overly melted/fused together, especially around the horn, pommel, and seat.

name: Chuck Wagon
defects: Long hitch/drawbar protrudes from the end with the canvas opening, making the wagon's front/rear orientation confusing and likely attached to the wrong end.
A partial extra wheel is visible under the left end, giving the wagon more than the expected two visible side wheels.
Undercarriage shapes are muddy/merged, with wheel supports and shadows blending together under the wagon.
Right-side storage cabinet appears fused into the wagon body rather than clearly mounted as a separate box.

name: Canvas Tent
defects: Right side canvas is a single flat rectangular sheet that does not wrap over a visible rear frame like a real tent.
Small wooden peg protrudes from the upper right canvas edge but is not connected to any visible pole or frame.
Rear support structure is incomplete: only one small rear leg is visible and there is no matching rear pole on the other side.
Front teepee-style crossed poles and side A-frame canvas are combined in an impossible construction.

name: Ore Cart
defects: The visible wheels do not sit cleanly on the rail heads; the rails appear slightly misaligned with or passing behind/through the wheel bottoms.
The rear wheels and axle are partial dark shapes and are not clearly connected to the cart frame.
The wheel brackets are fused into the lower cart body with unclear separate axle mounts.

name: Nugget Pouch
defects: Drawstring rope and knot are fused into simplified blob-like pieces rather than distinct strands passing through a real knot.
Cord appears to wrap into the bag fabric without visible holes, loops, or a proper channel.
Several gold nuggets are floating outside the bag with no contact or support, though they may be intended as spilling motion.

name: Miner Lantern
defects: Hook is attached off-center to a side pivot rather than centered above the lantern.
Top hook support is asymmetrical: one upright bracket is visible on the left, while the right side becomes a round lump/pivot.
Horizontal cage ring appears to pass through or fuse into the vertical ribs instead of being clearly joined.
Left outer side rail/handle is partly hidden and awkwardly fused into the lower side block, making the cage construction unclear.
Ventilation slots around the top are uneven in size and spacing.

name: Mine Headframe
defects: Central pulley wheel has no visible rope, groove, or functional winding path.
Metal hanger strap runs down the front of the wheel and into the hub, intersecting the wheel instead of forming a realistic axle bracket.
Pulley wheel appears fused to or pressed against the top beam with no clear clearance.
Wheel spokes are uneven in spacing and shape, with some spokes partly hidden or merged into the solid back disk.
The wheel is mounted on a solid wooden disk/plank surface rather than an open pulley/wheel construction.
Lower interior rails and box-like base form an ambiguous, partly enclosed opening that does not clearly connect to the pulley mechanism.

name: Ore Bucket
defects: Only one rope strand is visible from the pulley to the hook; there is no return/free rope end, so the pulley could not actually lift the bucket.
The hook and rope connection is simplified/melted together, with the rope ending directly into the hook instead of a clear knot or shackle.
